newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt likens Turkey buffer zone to Israel zone.
newsitem.headline: Egypt likens Turkey buffer zone to Israel zone.

text.p: Egypt on Sunday likened Turkey's planned security buffer zone in Kurdish northern Iraq to Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone and rejected Ankara's proposal as a violation of Iraq's sovereignity.

Turkey said last week it was planning to set up a security zone to keep out Turkish Kurdish rebels who use northern Iraq as a base for attacks on southeast Turkey where they are fighting for self-rule.

"This position reminds us of a similiar position when Israel announced the creation of a security zone in southern Lebanon with technical differences," Sayyed Qassem el-Masri, assistant foreign minister for multilateral relations, told reporters.
He was speaking after talks with Turkey's ambassador to Cairo, who Masri said had requested the meeting to explain Turkey's position.

Israeli troops, assisted by 3,000 Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army militia, have held a 15-km (nine-mile) wide zone in south Lebanon since 1985. Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas often attack the occupation troops.

Masri said he told the Turkish diplomat that Egypt rejected Turkey's explanations of its need to set up the zone and that Egypt would request an official discussion of the matter at the U.N. Security Council.

"I told the Turkish ambassador that Iraq's land is part of the Arab world and that the Egyptian and Arab people are upset by the double standards that are used by the international community against Arabs," Masri said.

"Egypt's position at the Security Council has been clear. It has expressed its deep worry about Turkey's decision to set up this buffer zone which can be considered a clear violation of Iraqi sovereignity and its regional safety," he added.
The United States has said it backs Turkey's plan as long as it is temporary but France and Russia have come out against the proposal.
Washington launched retaliatory raids against Iraqi military targets last week after Baghdad's troops entered Kurdish areas in northern Iraq to support a Kurdish rebel faction.
